architecture_decisions: - Model text never becomes mutation authority.
work_items: - The existing strict `TextPatchEngine` remains the final source patch verifier and committer.
validations: - A server-owned canonicalization layer may run only after an ordinary strict patch attempt fails for unified-diff format, exact-position conflict, or model-supplied base-digest mismatch.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — A currently valid strict single-file unified diff with the correct base digest continues to validate and apply exactly as before without canonicalization changing its bytes or result.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — For an existing safe text target, a proposal with exact context/deletion/addition intent but incorrect hunk counts or positions is converted to a canonical strict diff and accepted only when the source-consuming sequence matches exact protected source at one admissible location.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — When the declared old position points at an exact source-consuming sequence, that exact location is used even if equivalent text exists elsewhere; no search-based ambiguity is introduced.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — When the declared position is wrong, a hunk may relocate only if its complete source-consuming sequence has exactly one admissible non-overlapping exact match. Zero or multiple matches are rejected.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — An existing-file hunk containing additions only is never fuzzy-relocated. Its declared old position must be in bounds and non-overlapping, and a stale model-supplied base digest is not rebound when any such unanchored hunk exists.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — When every existing-file hunk consumes exact current protected source text, an incorrect model-supplied expected-base SHA-256 may be replaced only with the server-derived SHA-256 of that exact current target after canonicalization proves all anchors. The unchanged strict verifier must then accept the resulting patch before candidate admission.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — A new safe target may canonicalize addition-only diff intent only with `/dev/null` old-file semantics. The server-owned empty-base SHA, parent directory, extension, path, secret, size, and no-op protections remain unchanged.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Unsafe/secret path or content, unsupported extension, symlink, missing parent, oversized patch/result/source, ambiguous relocation, mismatching context/deletion text, overlapping hunks, unanchored stale-base insertion, multi-file intent, deletion/rename/mode-change intent, and malformed records remain rejected.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — Work Specification binding, acceptance-ID equality, candidate/worker ceilings, model order, source lineage acceptance, disposable candidate validation, Git/deployment authority and REVIEW boundary are unchanged.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — Runtime diagnostics may identify fixed canonicalization result/rejection classes and whether an anchored base digest was rebound without persisting raw model output, raw source text, provider payloads, credentials, or arbitrary exception messages.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — After deployment, replay at least one production path that previously ended `AGENTIC_CANDIDATE_EXHAUSTED` and require evidence that IMPLEMENT crosses the candidate safe-patch boundary. Simple Python/OT Time QA fixture success alone is insufficient acceptance evidence.
AC-12: validate protected requirement — `ARCHITECTURE.md` v3.30 records server-owned exact patch-intent canonicalization, anchored base-digest derivation, and the unchanged strict patch verifier.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Exact-head API/contracts, client/browser/Skia, Bounded Autonomy, protected promotion, Workstream Spec Validation, and DSPy release compilation pass before merge.

critique: The model text never becomes mutation authority. The existing strict `TextPatchEngine` remains the final source patch verifier and committer. A server-owned canonicalization layer may run only after an ordinary strict patch attempt fails for unified-diff format, exact-position conflict, or model-supplied base-digest mismatch. The canonicalization may repair only mechanical source-patch metadata: accepted path header prefix form, hunk counts, hunk coordinates, exact relocation of a hunk whose old/context record sequence exists unmodified in current protected source, and the model-supplied expected-base digest after exact source intent has been proven. The relocation uses exact string equality only. It may use the declared old position when that position exactly matches the hunk; otherwise, the complete old/context sequence must occur at exactly one admissible non-overlapping source position. No fuzzy text matching, edit-distance matching, semantic patching, approximate context, shell `patch`, Git apply, network tool, model, and other protected failures remain fail-closed.
